docs.text: HardFOC driver · ESP32 WS2812 RMT Driver ¶ A C++ driver for WS2812 and WS2812B addressable LEDs (NeoPixels) on the ESP32 family. It keeps a pixel buffer, scales brightness, encodes every bit as an RMT symbol and lets the RMT peripheral time the pulses, so the CPU never bit-bangs the line. Animation effects and multi-strip coordination come with it. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver is ESP-IDF code. Unlike the other HardFOC drivers it has no platform port: it calls ESP-IDF's RMT driver directly, so it runs on ESP32 chips with an RMT peripheral and ESP-IDF v5.3 or later, and nowhere else. Porting explains what that means for other targets. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , where Rgb(r, g, b) packs a colour as 0xRRGGBB , the format SetPixel() takes (see Colour order ). The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ Class Header Owns WS2812Strip ws2812_cpp.hpp One RMT channel, the pixel buffer, brightness, timing, LED type WS2812Animator ws2812_effects.hpp One effect on one strip: a step counter and a colour WS2812MultiAnimator ws2812_multi_animator.hpp One animator per strip, with a shared step ws2812::RmtTx rmt_wrapper.hpp An RMT transmit channel; raw symbols or WS2812 bytes WS2812Strip member Does WS2812Strip(gpio, channel, num_leds, type, t0h, t1h, t0l, t1l, brightness) Creates the RMT channel; every argument has a Kconfig default SetPixel(index, colour) Writes one pixel ( 0xRRGGBB , or 0xWWRRGGBB for RGBW); out-of-range indices are ignored Show() Scales, encodes and sends the buffer green first, then the reset; blocks until done; returns esp_err_t SetBrightness(0-255) Global scale applied at the next Show() SetNumLeds(n) Resizes and clears the buffer SetTimings(t0h, t1h, t0l, t1l) New bit timing in 100 ns ticks Length() The number of LEDs ColorWheel(0-255) A colour on a red-green-blue wheel, packed 0xRRGGBB Begin() ESP_OK if the constructor set the channel up, otherwise retries and returns the RMT error GetDriverVersion() The version string, for example "1.0.0" Create a strip ¶ // WS2812B timing in 100 ns ticks: T0H 400 ns, T1H 800 ns, T0L 900 ns, T1L 500 ns (also the Kconfig // defaults). WS2812Strip make_status_strip () { return WS2812Strip ( GPIO_NUM_8 , // data pin -1 , // channel: unused, ESP-IDF picks a free one 16 , // LEDs LedType :: RGB , // 24 bits per LED (LedType::RGBW: 32) 4 , 8 , 9 , 5 , // T0H, T1H, T0L, T1L in ticks 64 ); // brightness 0-255 } The constructor creates and enables the RMT channel at once. It does not abort when that fails (no free channel, an invalid GPIO, no memory); check Begin() before the first frame: bool start_strip ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { // The constructor does not abort when the channel cannot be created; Begin() says whether it was, // and tries again if not. const esp_err_t err = strip . Begin (); if ( err != ESP_OK ) { ESP_LOGE ( "leds" , "no RMT channel: %s" , esp_err_to_name ( err )); // e.g. ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND return false ; } return true ; } Until Begin() succeeds, Show() returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE . Keep the object alive as long as you use the LEDs: the destructor releases the channel. The channel argument is accepted and unused: ESP-IDF v5's RMT driver picks a free transmit channel and has no way to request a number. Set pixels and show them ¶ esp_err_t show_gradient ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { const uint32_t n = strip . Length (); const uint32_t last = n > 1 ? n - 1 : 1 ; for ( uint32_t i = 0 ; i < n ; ++ i ) { const auto level = static_cast < uint8_t > ( 255 * i / last ); strip . SetPixel ( i , Rgb ( level , 0 , 255 - level )); // blue to red } return strip . Show (); // nothing reaches the LEDs until Show() } SetPixel() only writes the buffer. Show() sends the whole strip every time; there is no partial update, and the LEDs keep their colours until the next frame. Dim the strip ¶ esp_err_t dim ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { strip . SetBrightness ( 16 ); // scales every channel of every LED at the next Show() return strip . Show (); } Each channel is scaled as value × brightness / 255 while encoding. The buffer keeps the full values, so raising the brightness again restores the colours exactly. At low brightness, small values round down to 0. Change the length ¶ esp_err_t grow ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { strip . SetNumLeds ( 60 ); // all pixels are cleared to 0 strip . SetPixel ( 59 , Rgb ( 0 , 0 , 255 )); return strip . Show (); } SetNumLeds() reallocates the pixel and symbol buffers and clears every pixel. Call it from the task that calls Show() . Change the timing ¶ void use_ws2812_original_timing ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { // 4, 8, 9, 5 already fit both parts. To centre on the WS2812's nominal 350 / 700 / 800 / 600 ns: strip . SetTimings ( 4 , 7 , 8 , 6 ); // T0H, T1H, T0L, T1L in ticks of 100 ns } The values are RMT ticks of 100 ns. Signal timing has the windows for the WS2812 and WS2812B. Animate ¶ void led_task ( void * arg ) { auto & strip = * static_cast < WS2812Strip *> ( arg ); WS2812Animator anim ( strip ); anim . SetEffect ( WS2812Animator :: Effect :: Rainbow ); for (;;) { anim . Tick (); // computes one frame and calls strip.Show() vTaskDelay ( pdMS_TO_TICKS ( 20 )); } } Effect Each Tick() Off Clears the strip SolidColor Sets every LED to the colour Rainbow Spreads ColorWheel() over the strip and shifts it by one step Chase Lights every third LED and moves the pattern by one Blink Alternates between the colour and off Breath Ramps the strip brightness up and down in steps of 4 (overwrites SetBrightness() ) Larson One lit LED that moves end to end and back Every Tick() ends with a Show() , so the tick rate is the frame rate; 20 ms (50 Hz) is smooth. Tick() ignores the result of Show() ; check transmit errors on the strip if you need them. SetVirtualLength() stretches an effect over a longer imaginary strip, and SetStep() / Step() read and set its position. Drive several strips ¶ void two_strips ( WS2812Strip & front , WS2812Strip & rear ) { // unified = true: both strips run the effect over the longer strip's length. // sync = true: one step counter for both. WS2812MultiAnimator multi ({ & front , & rear }, true , true ); multi . SetEffect ( WS2812Animator :: Effect :: Chase , Rgb ( 255 , 80 , 0 )); multi . SetEffect ( 1 , WS2812Animator :: Effect :: Blink , Rgb ( 255 , 0 , 0 )); // rear strip only for ( int frame = 0 ; frame < 500 ; ++ frame ) { multi . Tick (); vTaskDelay ( pdMS_TO_TICKS ( 50 )); } } Each strip has its own RMT channel and one memory block, so the number of strips is the chip's number of transmit channels ( Porting ). One strip too many fails in Begin() with ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND . The strips are sent one after the other in each Tick() . Handle errors ¶ bool show_or_report ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { const esp_err_t err = strip . Show (); if ( err != ESP_OK ) { // The RMT driver's code, or ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE when the channel was never set up. ESP_LOGE ( "leds" , "Show failed: %s" , esp_err_to_name ( err )); return false ; } return true ; } Signal Meaning What to do Begin() returns an error rmt_new_tx_channel() , rmt_enable() or the encoder failed: ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND (no free channel), a bad GPIO, no memory Fix the configuration, or free a channel and call Begin() again Show() returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE The channel was never set up Check Begin() Show() returns another esp_err_t The RMT driver refused the transfer Log it with esp_err_to_name() ; the frame was not sent Wrong colours, all white, flicker Timing, colour order or signal level, not a software error Troubleshooting Send bytes directly ¶ esp_err_t send_raw_grb ( ws2812 :: RmtTx & tx ) { // Bytes go out as they are, MSB first, with the WS2812B timing built into RmtTx (10 MHz // resolution): already in wire order, and no reset is appended. const uint8_t frame [] = { 0x00 , 0xFF , 0x00 , // LED 0: red (G, R, B) 0xFF , 0x00 , 0x00 }; // LED 1: green return tx . TransmitWs2812 ( frame , sizeof ( frame )); } ws2812::RmtTx can also be used on its own: TransmitWs2812() sends bytes as they are with the WS2812B timing, Transmit() sends prepared symbols and TransmitBytes() takes your own 0 and 1 symbols. All three block until the transfer is done, send no reset of their own, and return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE while IsReady() is false; InitStatus() holds the set-up error and Init() retries it. The C interface ¶ The C functions ws2812_control_init() , ws2812_write_leds() and ws2812_set_brightness() drive one strip whose LED type, length and timing come from Kconfig. struct led_state holds one 0xRRGGBB (or 0xWWRRGGBB ) value per LED; ws2812_write_leds() scales them by the brightness, sends them green first with the Kconfig timing, appends the 300 µs reset and blocks until done. It returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE before ws2812_control_init() , which can be called once (a second call returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE ) and cleans up after itself when it fails. The channel argument is unused. Prefer WS2812Strip for more than one strip. Threads ¶ The classes are not thread-safe. Give each strip one owner task, or guard every call on a strip (and on any animator that uses it) with one mutex.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: the layers from your application to the LEDs, what each owns, and how one frame reaches the strip. From pixels to pulses, on ESP-IDF Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application, the only code you write, either runs an effect or sets pixels itself. The effects (WS2812Animator and WS2812MultiAnimator, the Effect values listed from inc/ws2812_effects.hpp) draw into a WS2812Strip. The strip (inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp, public methods listed) keeps the pixel buffer, applies the brightness and turns every bit into one RMT symbol with the configured high and low times. ws2812::RmtTx (inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp) owns one RMT transmit channel at 10 MHz and sends the symbols, blocking until they are out. Below it is ESP-IDF's RMT driver (the calls listed from rmt_wrapper.hpp) and the RMT peripheral, which times the pulses on the GPIO that feeds the first LED. Drawn from: inc/ws2812_effects.hpp WS2812Animator::Effect ; inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp WS2812Strip ; inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp ws2812::RmtTx ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The layers ¶ Layer Where You change it when Effects : WS2812Animator , WS2812MultiAnimator ws2812_effects.hpp , ws2812_multi_animator.hpp You want a new effect Strip : WS2812Strip ws2812_cpp.hpp , ws2812_cpp.cpp Never, for a new board RMT channel : ws2812::RmtTx rmt_wrapper.hpp Never ESP-IDF RMT driver and the peripheral ESP-IDF, esp_driver_rmt Never Each layer uses only the one below it. There is no communication interface for you to implement. The other HardFOC drivers talk to a chip over a bus your port provides; a WS2812 has no bus, only a pulse train with 100 ns resolution, and the RMT peripheral is what makes that possible on an ESP32 without blocking the CPU. Porting explains the consequences. How one frame reaches the strip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant S as WS2812Strip participant T as RmtTx participant R as ESP-IDF RMT A->>S: SetPixel(i, colour), for each LED A->>S: Show() S->>S: scale by brightness, one symbol per bit S->>T: Transmit(symbols, count) T->>R: rmt_transmit(copy encoder) T->>R: rmt_tx_wait_all_done() R-->>T: ESP_OK when the last symbol is out T-->>S: esp_err_t S-->>A: esp_err_t Show() blocks the calling task for the whole frame: about 31 µs per RGB LED with the WS2812B timing ( Signal timing ). The RMT sends the symbols on its own; the CPU only refills the channel's symbol memory from an interrupt. Design choices ¶ Symbols built in software, sent with a copy encoder. Show() writes one rmt_symbol_word_t per bit into a buffer the strip owns, then the RMT copies them out. The timing is plain data, so SetTimings() takes effect at the next Show() and the host tests can check every pulse. One RMT channel per strip, created in the constructor. The channel takes one memory block of the target. A failure to create it does not abort: Begin() returns the error and retries, and Show() returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE until the channel is up ( Troubleshooting ). Wire order inside the driver. Pixels are 0xRRGGBB ; Show() reorders to green, red, blue and appends the reset symbol, so callers never pack for the wire. Brightness at send time. Pixels are stored unscaled; brightness is applied while encoding, so dimming and restoring never loses colour resolution in the buffer. Effects are separate. The strip knows nothing about animation. An animator draws one frame per Tick() and calls Show() ; you decide when to tick. Heap at construction, not per frame. The strip allocates its pixel and symbol buffers ( std::vector ) when it is created or resized; Show() does not allocate. The C interface ¶ inc/ws2812_control.h is an older C interface for one strip whose length, LED type and timing are fixed by Kconfig. It does not share code with WS2812Strip : it sends pixel bytes through led_strip_encoder.c , which appends the reset ( API guide ). docs.text: How the driver is put together: the layers from your application to the LEDs, what each owns, and how one frame reaches the strip. From pixels to pulses, on ESP-IDF Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application, the only code you write, either runs an effect or sets pixels itself. The effects (WS2812Animator and WS2812MultiAnimator, the Effect values listed from inc/ws2812_effects.hpp) draw into a WS2812Strip. The strip (inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp, public methods listed) keeps the pixel buffer, applies the brightness and turns every bit into one RMT symbol with the configured high and low times. ws2812::RmtTx (inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp) owns one RMT transmit channel at 10 MHz and sends the symbols, blocking until they are out. Below it is ESP-IDF's RMT driver (the calls listed from rmt_wrapper.hpp) and the RMT peripheral, which times the pulses on the GPIO that feeds the first LED. Drawn from: inc/ws2812_effects.hpp WS2812Animator::Effect ; inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp WS2812Strip ; inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp ws2812::RmtTx ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py .

There is no communication interface for you to implement. The other HardFOC drivers talk to a chip over a bus your port provides; a WS2812 has no bus, only a pulse train with 100 ns resolution, and the RMT peripheral is what makes that possible on an ESP32 without blocking the CPU. docs.text: sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant S as WS2812Strip participant T as RmtTx participant R as ESP-IDF RMT A->>S: SetPixel(i, colour), for each LED A->>S: Show() S->>S: scale by brightness, one symbol per bit S->>T: Transmit(symbols, count) T->>R: rmt_transmit(copy encoder) T->>R: rmt_tx_wait_all_done() R-->>T: ESP_OK when the last symbol is out T-->>S: esp_err_t S-->>A: esp_err_t Show() blocks the calling task for the whole frame: about 31 µs per RGB LED with the WS2812B timing ( Signal timing ). The RMT sends the symbols on its own; the CPU only refills the channel's symbol memory from an interrupt.

docs.text: Symbols built in software, sent with a copy encoder. Show() writes one rmt_symbol_word_t per bit into a buffer the strip owns, then the RMT copies them out. The timing is plain data, so SetTimings() takes effect at the next Show() and the host tests can check every pulse. One RMT channel per strip, created in the constructor. The channel takes one memory block of the target. A failure to create it does not abort: Begin() returns the error and retries, and Show() returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE until the channel is up ( Troubleshooting ). Wire order inside the driver. Pixels are 0xRRGGBB ; Show() reorders to green, red, blue and appends the reset symbol, so callers never pack for the wire. Brightness at send time. Pixels are stored unscaled; brightness is applied while encoding, so dimming and restoring never loses colour resolution in the buffer. Effects are separate. The strip knows nothing about animation. An animator draws one frame per Tick() and calls Show() ; you decide when to tick. Heap at construction, not per frame. The strip allocates its pixel and symbol buffers ( std::vector ) when it is created or resized; Show() does not allocate.

docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries marked BREAKING need source changes in code that used the affected API. [Unreleased] ¶ Breaking ¶ WS2812Strip::Show() sends green first. Pixels are 0xRRGGBB ( 0xWWRRGGBB for RGBW) and go out in the WS2812B order G, R, B (then W, the SK6812RGBW order). Before, the packed value went out as it was, so red came first and RGBW sent white first. Code that packed 0xGGRRBB to work around it now swaps red and green: pack 0xRRGGBB and drop the workaround. ColorWheel() and the effects now show their intended colours. Kconfig timing defaults are WS2812B values in 100 ns ticks ( CONFIG_WS2812_T0H/T1H/T0L/T1L = 4, 8, 9, 5, was 14, 52, 52, 52, which a WS2812B read as all ones). Constructor calls without timing arguments and the C interface change output. A project sdkconfig keeps old values until you edit it. ws2812::RmtTx and WS2812Strip no longer abort when the RMT channel cannot be created. WS2812Strip::Begin() returns the error (and retries) instead of always ESP_OK ; until it succeeds Show() returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE . Check Begin() where you relied on the abort. ws2812_control_init() returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE when called a second time (it used to leak a channel), and ws2812_write_leds() before init returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE . Fixed ¶ ws2812_write_leds() sent the bytes of its RMT symbol buffer through the byte encoder instead of the colours; it now sends the pixel bytes in wire order with the Kconfig timing and a reset. Show() sends a reset (line low for WS2812Strip::kResetTimeUs = 300 µs, WS2812B-V5 needs at least 280 µs) after every frame, so back-to-back frames latch. Each strip requests one RMT memory block of the target ( SOC_RMT_MEM_WORDS_PER_CHANNEL : 48 symbols on S3, C3, C6, H2) instead of 64 symbols, which took two blocks there and left no memory for a second strip on the two-channel chips. Override with WS2812_RMT_MEM_BLOCK_SYMBOLS . ws2812_control_init() releases the channel and encoder when a later step fails. CMake: install rules for the library, headers and generated version header, an exported hf::hf_ws2812_rmt target and a package config that works after install (it included an uninstalled file); the project version comes from the build settings. The ESP32 example is a real hardware test (colours, brightness, animation, two strips) instead of a placeholder; its config header compiles. Added ¶ ws2812::RmtTx::Init() , InitStatus() , IsReady() ; WS2812Strip::kResetTimeUs ; ws2812_rmt_caps.h . led_strip_encoder_config_t takes optional bit times and reset length (0 keeps the WS2812B defaults, now 400/850/800/450 ns and 300 µs instead of 300/900/900/300 ns and 50 µs). docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between an ESP32 and a WS2812B strip, the signal it expects, and how to power it. The numbers here come from the Worldsemi WS2812B datasheet and, for the original WS2812, the WS2812 datasheet . Clones and later revisions differ; check the datasheet of the LEDs you bought. Pins ¶ Pin Name Connect to 1 VDD 5 V supply (3.5 V to 5.3 V) 2 DOUT (out) DIN of the next LED 3 VSS Supply ground and ESP32 ground 4 DIN (in) ESP32 GPIO, through a level shifter A strip brings out VDD (often labelled 5V or +), DIN and GND at its input end. The data goes one way: connect the end marked DIN or with the arrow pointing away from the connector. The ESP32 side ¶ Setting Value Notes Peripheral One RMT transmit channel Chosen by ESP-IDF's RMT driver; the channel argument is unused GPIO Any output-capable GPIO GPIO8 in the examples (ESP32-C6) Resolution 10 MHz, 100 ns per tick Fixed by WS2812Strip Symbol memory One block (64 symbols on ESP32/S2, 48 on S3/C3/C6/H2), no DMA Refilled by interrupt while a frame is sent Output level 3.3 V Below the WS2812B's 3.5 V high threshold at 5 V Signal ¶ The LEDs read one line, non-return-to-zero at 800 kbit/s. Every bit is a high pulse followed by a low one; the length of the high pulse decides 0 or 1. Each LED keeps the first 24 bits it receives and passes the rest on through DOUT, reshaped. A low line for longer than the reset time latches the new colours into every LED. Parameter WS2812B Driver (100 ns ticks) T0H, 0 bit high 0.40 µs ±150 ns 4: 0.4 µs T1H, 1 bit high 0.80 µs ±150 ns 8: 0.8 µs T0L, 0 bit low 0.85 µs ±150 ns 9: 0.9 µs T1L, 1 bit low 0.45 µs ±150 ns 5: 0.5 µs TH + TL 1.25 µs ±600 ns 1.3 µs Reset, line low more than 50 µs (WS2812B-V5: at least 280 µs) 300 µs after every frame ( reset ) Bit order G7 ... G0, R7 ... R0, B7 ... B0 Green byte first from a 0xRRGGBB pixel, MSB first The original WS2812 specifies 0.35, 0.7, 0.8 and 0.6 µs, each ±150 ns, and the same reset and order; the driver values above fall inside both parts' windows. The driver column is the Kconfig default and what the examples on this site pass to the constructor ( Configuration ). sequenceDiagram participant E as ESP32 (RMT) participant L0 as LED 0 participant L1 as LED 1 E->>L0: 24 bits for LED 0, then 24 for LED 1 L0->>L0: keep the first 24 bits L0->>L1: forward the rest through DOUT E->>L0: reset: line low for 300 µs L0->>L0: latch: new colour shows L1->>L1: latch: new colour shows Signal timing turns these numbers into ticks, frame times and memory. Logic levels ¶ Parameter WS2812B At VDD = 5 V VIH, input high 0.7 × VDD minimum 3.5 V VIL, input low 0.3 × VDD maximum 1.5 V Input voltage −0.5 V to VDD + 0.5 V 3.3 V data into a 5 V strip An ESP32's 3.3 V high is under the 3.5 V the datasheet asks for. Many strips accept it on a short wire, some do not, and the margin shrinks with temperature and cable length. Use a buffer powered from 5 V that accepts 3.3 V inputs (74AHCT125, 74HCT245) between the GPIO and DIN. Power ¶ Item Value Source VDD 3.5 V to 5.3 V WS2812B datasheet Current at full white About 60 mA per LED Three LEDs at 20 mA each, from the WS2812 datasheet; the WS2812B datasheet gives no figure Decoupling 100 nF at each LED WS2812B application circuit (most strips have it) Operating temperature −25 °C to +80 °C WS2812B datasheet Budget the supply for the strip: 60 LEDs at full white is about 3.6 A. Brightness scaling lowers it in proportion. Feed long strips from both ends or every metre or so, so the far LEDs do not dim or shift colour. docs.text: Porting ¶ What runs where: the driver is ESP-IDF code for the ESP32 family. This page lists the chips it supports, what binds it to ESP-IDF, and what using it elsewhere would take. Why there is no port to write ¶ The other HardFOC drivers talk to a chip over SPI, I2C or UART, so they ask you for a small class that moves bytes, and run on any MCU. A WS2812 has no bus: it needs a pulse train timed to about 100 ns for the whole frame. On an ESP32 the RMT peripheral generates it from a buffer of symbols. This driver is built around that peripheral and calls ESP-IDF's RMT driver directly; there is no interface between the two for you to implement. Supported chips ¶ The component manifest lists these targets. The channel and memory figures are ESP-IDF's ( soc_caps.h , v5.5). Chip Transmit channels Symbols per block ESP32 8 (any channel) 64 ESP32-S2 4 (any channel) 64 ESP32-S3 4 48 ESP32-C3 2 48 ESP32-C6 2 48 ESP32-H2 2 48 CI builds the examples for the ESP32-C6 with ESP-IDF v5.5; the other chips are listed by the manifest but not built. Each WS2812Strip (and the C interface) asks ESP-IDF for one transmit channel with one memory block of the target ( SOC_RMT_MEM_WORDS_PER_CHANNEL ), so every transmit channel of the chip can drive a strip. Define WS2812_RMT_MEM_BLOCK_SYMBOLS before including the driver to ask for more; above one block a channel takes its neighbour's block too. Chips without an RMT peripheral (the ESP32-C2, for example) cannot run it. ESP-IDF v5.3 or later is required, because the component requires esp_driver_rmt . What is bound to ESP-IDF ¶ File ESP-IDF dependency inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp The RMT TX and RX driver, encoders, esp_check.h , esp_log.h , FreeRTOS queues inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp , src/ws2812_cpp.cpp gpio_num_t , esp_err_t , rmt_symbol_word_t , Kconfig defaults ( sdkconfig.h ) inc/ws2812_effects.hpp , inc/ws2812_multi_animator.hpp Only through WS2812Strip inc/ws2812_control.h , src/*.c The RMT driver and Kconfig, directly The effects and the bit encoding in WS2812Strip::Show() are plain C++; the ESP-IDF parts are the channel in ws2812::RmtTx and the types in the public headers. Using it on another MCU ¶ There is no supported path. Doing it means: Replacing ws2812::RmtTx with a transmitter for your MCU that sends a buffer of (high time, low time) pairs: a timer with DMA, an SPI peripheral clocked so that a few SPI bits make one WS2812 bit, or a PIO block. Replacing the ESP-IDF types in the public headers ( gpio_num_t , esp_err_t , rmt_symbol_word_t ) and the Kconfig defaults. The host build in tests/stubs/ shows the full set of ESP-IDF names the driver uses: it is a starting point, not a port. For a non-ESP32 project, a library written for your MCU's timing peripheral is usually less work. Using it on any ESP32 ¶ Nothing to write: the component wrapper builds it. Check that the GPIO is an output on your chip, that you have a free RMT transmit channel per strip, and pass WS2812B timing to the constructor ( Configuration ). Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each strip one owner task, or guard every call on a strip and its animators with one mutex. Show() blocks its caller for the length of a frame; strips on different channels can be sent from different tasks.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Light a WS2812B strip from an ESP32: wire three signals, add the component, write one loop. ESP32 and ESP-IDF only The driver calls ESP-IDF's RMT driver directly. You need an ESP32-family chip with an RMT peripheral and ESP-IDF v5.3 or later; CI builds the examples for the ESP32-C6 with ESP-IDF v5.5. 1. Wire it ¶ ESP32 Strip Notes GPIO (GPIO8 in the example) DIN of the first LED Through a 3.3 V to 5 V level shifter; see below GND GND (VSS) One ground for the ESP32, the strip and its supply 5 V (VDD) From a supply sized for the strip: up to about 60 mA per LED at full white A WS2812B powered from 5 V needs at least 3.5 V (0.7 × VDD) on DIN to see a high. An ESP32 drives 3.3 V, which is below that: it often works on a short wire, but it is out of specification. A 74AHCT125 or 74HCT245 powered from 5 V fixes it. Hardware has the pin table, the power budget and the protection parts. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and copy the ESP-IDF component wrapper into your project's components/ folder. Installation has the details and the alternatives. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver.git external/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver cp -r external/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver/examples/esp32/components/hf_ws2812_rmt components/ Tell the wrapper where the driver is, in your top-level CMakeLists.txt before the project.cmake include, and add hf_ws2812_rmt to the REQUIRES of your main component: set ( HF_WS2812_RMT_ROOT ${ CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR } /external/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver CACHE PATH "WS2812 driver checkout" ) 3. Light it ¶ main.cpp #include "esp_log.h" #include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h" #include "freertos/task.h" #include "ws2812_cpp.hpp" // WS2812B bit timing in RMT ticks of 100 ns (the driver runs the RMT at 10 MHz). constexpr uint16_t kT0H = 4 , kT1H = 8 , kT0L = 9 , kT1L = 5 ; extern "C" void app_main () { // 8 LEDs on GPIO8, brightness 32 of 255. The constructor claims an RMT TX channel. WS2812Strip strip ( GPIO_NUM_8 , -1 , 8 , LedType :: RGB , kT0H , kT1H , kT0L , kT1L , 32 ); if ( strip . Begin () != ESP_OK ) { // no free RMT channel, or a bad GPIO ESP_LOGE ( "leds" , "RMT channel set-up failed" ); return ; } for ( uint32_t i = 0 ;; i = ( i + 1 ) % strip . Length ()) { strip . SetPixel ( i , 0xFF0000 ); // 0xRRGGBB: one red LED walks along the strip if ( strip . Show () != ESP_OK ) { // blocks until the frame is on the wire ESP_LOGE ( "leds" , "RMT transmit failed" ); } strip . SetPixel ( i , 0 ); vTaskDelay ( pdMS_TO_TICKS ( 100 )); } } What each step does: The WS2812Strip constructor creates an RMT transmit channel on the GPIO at 10 MHz, so the four timing arguments are in ticks of 100 ns: 4, 8, 9 and 5 give 400, 800, 900 and 500 ns, inside the WS2812B's ±150 ns window. They are also the Kconfig defaults ( Configuration ). Begin() reports whether the RMT channel was set up; a failure (no free channel, a bad GPIO) is returned, not an abort. Colours are packed 0xRRGGBB ; the driver sends green first, as a WS2812B expects. SetPixel() writes the buffer; nothing reaches the LEDs until Show() , which scales by the brightness, encodes 24 symbols per LED, appends the reset that latches the frame and blocks until the RMT has sent them. The host CI compiles this example against the driver's headers, so it matches the current API. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check Every LED white or full on The timing arguments: ticks are 100 ns, so values in ns or µs are far too long Red and green swapped Colour packing: SetPixel() takes 0xRRGGBB ; drop any 0xGGRRBB workaround from older code Nothing lights Ground shared with the strip, data into DIN (not DOUT), the GPIO number First LED flickers or shows random colours Data level: add the level shifter, keep the data wire short Begin() fails No free RMT transmit channel, or an invalid GPIO ( Troubleshooting ) Next ¶ API guide : brightness, resizing, effects, several strips, errors. docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host unit tests over a fake of ESP-IDF's RMT driver, compiled documentation, the ESP32 build and static analysis, on every pull request. docs.text: Signal timing ¶ How the driver turns pixels into pulses: ticks, the time a frame takes, the memory it needs and the reset gap. Ticks ¶ WS2812Strip runs its RMT channel at 10 MHz, so every duration it sends is a whole number of 100 ns ticks. The four timing arguments ( t0h , t1h , t0l , t1l ) are those tick counts, used as they are: the driver does not convert from nanoseconds. Pulse Driver value WS2812B window 0 bit high, t0h 4: 400 ns 250-550 ns 0 bit low, t0l 9: 900 ns 700-1000 ns 1 bit high, t1h 8: 800 ns 650-950 ns 1 bit low, t1l 5: 500 ns 300-600 ns Any value inside the window works; the LED samples the line roughly in the middle of the bit, so the difference between a short and a long high pulse is what matters. The Kconfig defaults are the values in the table (4, 8, 9, 5), so a strip created without timing arguments is right for a WS2812B. ws2812::RmtTx::TransmitWs2812() , the lower-level byte path, has its own fixed timing for 10 MHz: 400 / 900 ns for a 0 and 800 / 500 ns for a 1, the same as the table. Frame time ¶ Each LED takes 24 bits (32 for RGBW). With the timing above every bit lasts 1.3 µs: LEDs RGB frame Highest refresh rate 8 0.25 ms about 1800 Hz 60 1.9 ms about 460 Hz 144 4.5 ms about 210 Hz 300 9.4 ms about 104 Hz An RGBW frame is a third longer (32 bits instead of 24). The refresh rate allows for the frame and the 300 µs reset Show() sends after it. These numbers are derived from the bit time, not measured; Show() also spends CPU time building the symbols before the transfer starts. Show() blocks the calling task until the last symbol is out ( rmt_tx_wait_all_done() with no timeout). Call it from a task that can afford the wait, never from an interrupt. Memory ¶ Buffer Bytes per LED Pixels ( uint32_t ) 4 RMT symbols, RGB (24 × 4 bytes) 96 RMT symbols, RGBW (32 × 4 bytes) 128 A 60-LED RGB strip needs 6004 bytes: the symbol buffer has one more symbol for the reset. Both are std::vector s allocated when the strip is created or resized. The RMT channel itself has one memory block of hardware memory (64 symbols on the ESP32 and ESP32-S2, 48 on the S3, C3, C6 and H2) and no DMA; ESP-IDF refills it from an interrupt while a frame is sent. A refill delayed by a long critical section stretches a low period, which the LEDs read as a reset or a wrong bit. If you see glitches under heavy interrupt load, keep strips short or send frames from a high-priority task. The reset gap ¶ A WS2812B shows the new colours once its data line has stayed low for the reset time: more than 50 µs in the WS2812B datasheet, at least 280 µs for the WS2812B-V5 (80 µs for the SK6812). WS2812Strip::Show() ends every frame with a low symbol of WS2812Strip::kResetTimeUs (300 µs), which covers all of them, and returns only after it has been sent. Show() calls back to back are therefore safe. The C interface's encoder ( led_strip_encoder.c ) appends the same 300 µs reset. ws2812::RmtTx::TransmitWs2812() sends only the bytes you give it; leave 300 µs before the next call. Colour order ¶ Pixels are packed 0xRRGGBB : SetPixel(i, 0xFF0000) is red. A WS2812B reads green, red, blue (datasheet "Composition of 24bit data": G7 ... G0, R7 ... R0, B7 ... B0), so Show() sends the green byte, then red, then blue, each most significant bit first. ColorWheel() and the effects use the same packing. For an RGBW strip pack 0xWWRRGGBB ; Show() sends green, red, blue, then white, the order of the SK6812RGBW.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see when bringing up a WS2812 strip with this driver, their causes and the fix for each. Start with the cheapest check: a common ground, data into DIN of the first LED, and the timing arguments. Most faults are one of those three. Every LED is white, or full on in one colour ¶ Cause. The bit timing. WS2812Strip counts in ticks of 100 ns; values in microseconds or nanoseconds, or a project sdkconfig still holding the defaults of 1.0.0 and earlier (14, 52, 52, 52), make every high pulse too long, and the LEDs read every bit as a 1. Fix. Use WS2812B timing ( 4, 8, 9, 5 , the Kconfig default): pass it to the constructor or fix the CONFIG_WS2812_T* lines in sdkconfig ( Configuration ). Red and green are swapped ¶ Cause. Colour packing. SetPixel() takes 0xRRGGBB and the driver sends green first, as a WS2812B expects. Code written for 1.0.0 and earlier packed 0xGGRRBB to work around the old byte order; with this version that swaps red and green. A strip whose LEDs read R, G, B (some clones) shows the same symptom. Fix. Pack 0xRRGGBB and drop any Grb() -style helper ( Colour order ). For an RGB-order clone, swap the bytes before SetPixel() . Nothing lights ¶ Check How Ground The ESP32, the strip and the strip's supply share one ground Direction Data goes into DIN of the first LED, not DOUT of the last Supply 3.5 V to 5.3 V at the strip; measure at the far end under load GPIO The pin passed to the constructor is the one wired; it is an output on your chip Brightness Not 0, and not left at 0 by a Breath effect you stopped Show() Called after SetPixel() , and its result is ESP_OK The first LED flickers or shows random colours; the rest follow it ¶ Cause. The data level or the wire. A 3.3 V high is below the WS2812B's 3.5 V threshold at 5 V, and a long or unterminated data wire rings. Fix. Add a 5 V buffer such as a 74AHCT125, keep the data wire short, and put a 300 Ω to 500 Ω resistor in series with DIN at the strip ( Hardware ). The last LEDs keep old colours, or frames merge ¶ Cause. Not the reset: Show() ends every frame with a 300 µs low, longer than any WS2812-family part needs. The usual reasons are a frame shorter than the strip ( SetNumLeds() smaller than the LED count), or a supply or data problem at the point where the old colours start. Fix. Set the strip length to the real LED count, then check the supply and data wire at that LED. If you send raw bytes with ws2812::RmtTx::TransmitWs2812() , leave 300 µs between calls yourself ( Signal timing ). Colours fade or shift towards the far end ¶ Cause. Voltage drop along the strip at high current. Fix. Lower the brightness, or feed the supply in at both ends or every metre or so ( Hardware ). Begin() fails, or Show() returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE ¶ Cause. The strip's RMT channel could not be set up; the log names rmt_new_tx_channel , rmt_enable or the encoder. Usual reasons: no free transmit channel ( ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND : each strip takes one), an invalid GPIO, or out of memory. Fix. Create fewer strips, check the GPIO, and see Supported chips for the channel counts. Begin() retries, so it succeeds once a channel is free. Glitches while Wi-Fi or other interrupts are busy ¶ Cause. The RMT channel has one memory block (48 or 64 symbols) and no DMA; ESP-IDF refills it from an interrupt during a frame. A late refill stretches a low period. Fix. Keep strips short, send frames from a high-priority task, and avoid long critical sections while Show() runs ( Signal timing ). The C functions in ws2812_control.h send garbage ¶ Cause. Version 1.0.0 and earlier passed the RMT symbol buffer of ws2812_write_leds() to a byte encoder. Fixed since; with this version, garbage from the C interface means the Kconfig timing or LED type is wrong. Fix. Check CONFIG_WS2812_T* and CONFIG_WS2812_LED_TYPE_* ( Configuration ), or use WS2812Strip ( API guide ).
